# Published regression aggregate: FDI and unemployment

This local proposal is a small, derived published-aggregate extraction from Table 1 of the article **Relationship between FDI Inflow and Unemployment Rate in the Case of the Former Yugoslav Republics** (Balkan JETSS, 2024, pp. 11–20; DOI [10.31410/balkans.jetss.2024.7.1.11-20](https://doi.org/10.31410/balkans.jetss.2024.7.1.11-20)). It is not the study's source observations, a replication dataset, or a UIST deposit.

The CSV transcribes the six country rows and seven reported regression fields exactly as printed: intercept, FDI coefficient, R-squared, adjusted R-squared, correlation coefficient, p-value and F-test. Values were checked against the rendered article page containing Table 1 (printed page 15; PDF page 5) on 4 October 2026. The article describes unemployment data from the World Bank indicator `SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS` and FDI data from the UNCTAD World Investment Database for 1990–2021. Those source observations are not included here.

The article identifies the source calculations as the authors' and states a CC BY-NC 4.0 article licence. The proposed package should retain that attribution and non-commercial limitation unless UIST obtains an item-specific rights decision. The accountable compiler/depositor is unassigned; repository preparation transcribed the table; no author endorsement or depositor authority is implied. Original author identities, source links and the article DOI must remain in any accepted metadata.

Known limits: this is one reported table; denominators, country-year rows, preprocessing, R code, missingness and model diagnostics are unavailable in the package. Decimal precision is preserved as printed, including trailing zeroes where shown. The package is `prepared_needs_deposit` pending a responsible authorised compiler/depositor, source rights/access confirmation, normal deposit terms, metadata/identifier choices and public access checks.


Table1 does not specify coefficient units. No unit conversion or model recalculation was made. Its source numeric/statistical inconsistencies remain published values requiring scientific interpretation by a researcher. The source title omits “Rate” while current metadata includes it; same DOI/authors identify the article.
